name: assess_reachable
description:
OFFLINE manipulation-prep judgment: given a target and the accumulated scene (past trajectory /

memory), decide whether the agent can reach a position from which it can OPERATE the target —
WITHOUT any env step. Pure geometry + label heuristics, no VLM. Three outcomes: `reachable_now` (an
observed viewpoint is already within max_reach_m), `reachable_after_move` (target grounded but too
far → single-leg turn+go_forward plan + distance to close), or `target_not_grounded` (never observed
→ defer to assess_coverage / plan_exploration to FIND it first). Scope: judges only whether an
operable vantage is reachable, NOT whether the manipulation succeeds. Returns offline_assessment
(evidence_sufficiency / recommended_action / specific_data_calls / fallback_answer_hint) in the same
shape as plan_exploration.

target.description: Object to reach / operate on (e.g. 'cup', 'door handle', 'drawer').

max_reach_m.description:
Operable reach in meters: target counts as 'operable' if some observed viewpoint is
within this distance.

name: build_scene
description:
Assemble an instance-level 3D scene from objects YOU (the model) grounded + depth-estimated in each

frame — NO perception model runs here, it is pure geometry. Returns a `scene` JSON (instances +
camera poses + intrinsics + frame paths) that visualize_bev / triangulate / object_world_motion /
calibrate_scale / render_scene_views take back as their `scene` argument. Geometry is a COARSE
scaffold (depth_m is your estimate), not metric-accurate.

frames.description:
Absolute paths to the RGB frame images, aligned 1:1 with objects_by_frame (used for
image size + carried for render tools).

frame_indices.description: Original video frame indices per frame (default: 0..N-1).

is_video.description: Whether frames come from a video (vs still images).

camera_motions.description:
Per adjacent-frame camera motion (frame i→i+1), YOUR estimate. One entry per gap
= len(frames)-1. Each: {yaw_deg:+right/-left horizontal turn, forward_m:+forward/-back
planar meters, right_m:+right/-left planar meters, pitch_deg?:+up/-down tilt (recorded, NOT
used in c2w — BEV is ground-plane 3-DoF)}. Omit → identity cameras (single-view / static).

bbox_format.description:
Coordinate units for every box: normalized_1000 (default), normalized (0..1),
or pixels. Units are explicit, independent of image resolution.

name: calibrate_scale
description:
Refine absolute metric scale from a target's KNOWN real size: returns scale_factor = known_m /

observed_m. Multiply reconstructed depths/distances by it to correct absolute meters (monocular
depth_m alone gets absolute distance wrong). Needs a `scene` from build_scene.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene (alternative to `scene`).

target.description: Label of the object whose real-world size is known.

known_size_m.description: The object's known real size in meters (e.g. a chair ~0.5 m wide).

dim.description: Which dimension known_size_m refers to: 'width' or 'height'.

frame.description: Frame to measure the observed size in (default: first available).

name: camera_motion
description:
How the CAMERA moved between two frames, from the scene's camera poses (pure geometry): translation

(meters), rotation (yaw/pitch/roll deg), total rotation, and dominant direction (e.g. yaw-left,
moved-forward). Answers 'which way did the camera move/turn?'. Needs a `scene`.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene (alternative to `scene`).

name: count_objects
description:
Count objects from the scene's grounded instances (not a bare VLM guess). With `frame` → count in

that frame; without → count UNIQUE physical objects across all frames with BEV dedup (avoids double-
counting the same object seen in multiple frames). Optionally filter by `label`.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene.

label.description: Only count objects of this label (default: all).

frame.description:
Count in this single frame. If omitted, counts unique objects across ALL frames (BEV-
deduplicated).

dup_threshold.description: BEV dedup distance (meters) for across-frames counting.

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: assess_coverage
description:
Report how much of the world has been observed and whether that is sufficient to answer the current

question. Pure geometry + label heuristics — no VLM. Returns: coverage_deg (total angular sweep),
unobserved_sectors (world-heading gaps), candidate_gateways (door/corridor/opening items with
headings from the reference camera), known_rooms (guessed from seen labels), target_hint (likely
rooms for `target` from a small prior), and sufficient_for_target (true if target is already in
scene, else false).

target.description:
Optional: object label we want to find. If given, the tool also reports whether the
accumulated scene is enough (target present) or hints where it likely is (via room prior).

name: match_entities
description:
Cross-frame identity: group all sightings of an object across frames/views into unique physical

entities ('match_across_views'), or just count distinct objects ('deduplicate'). Use to avoid
double-counting the same object seen from multiple frames. Needs a `scene`.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene.

op.description:
'match_across_views' (group sightings into entities) or 'deduplicate' (count distinct
physical objects).

match_dist_m.description: BEV distance (meters) under which two sightings are the same object.

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: mobile_manip
description:
Embodied / mobile-manipulation over the scene. Two families of ops:   Observation:

`track_object_trajectory` (cross-frame BEV path), `check_object_in_view`, `suggest_approach`
(staging), `search_object_across_frames`, `reachability`.   Action-planning (pure geometry, no VLM):
`plan_navigation` gives a single-leg turn+forward sequence to a visible target; `plan_movement`
gates that behind a reachability check; `plan_active_search` handles the target-not-visible case —
from the camera trajectory, decide the next locomotion move (turn to an unobserved side, or
advance). Needs a `scene` from build_scene.

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene.

op.description:
Which routine to run. Observation/grounding: `track_object_trajectory` |
`check_object_in_view` | `suggest_approach` | `search_object_across_frames` |
`reachability`. Action planning: `plan_navigation` (single-leg turn+forward),
`plan_movement` (nav only if not reachable), `plan_active_search` (target NOT in scene →
suggest next scan move).

target.description: The object to reason about (label or instance id). Required for all ops.

frame.description: Frame index for ops that accept one (default: first).

model.description: Override VLM model (default: from env). Only affects VLM-backed ops.

name: motion
description:
Two pure-compute modes: (1) motion SEGMENTATION across a clip — pass `frames` to get which

regions/frames contain motion (frame-difference based); (2) trajectory EXTRAPOLATION — pass
`past_points` to fit and predict `n_future` points. Reason about motion in world/metric terms, not
raw pixels.

frames.description: Paths to frame images, in order — for motion segmentation across the clip.

motion_threshold.description: Optional motion threshold for segmentation (default: auto).

past_points.description:
A past 2D/3D track [[x,y(,z)], ...] — when given, extrapolate future points instead
of segmenting.

n_future.description: Number of future points to extrapolate (predict mode).

order.description: Polynomial fit order for extrapolation (predict mode).

name: object_world_motion
description:
Motion of `target` in the WORLD frame between two frames, with the camera's own ego-motion REMOVED —

distinguishes 'the object moved' from 'the camera moved'. Returns displacement_m / direction /
is_moving / camera_moved_m. Never infer motion from pixel shift; use this. Needs a `scene` from
build_scene.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene (alternative to `scene`).

target.description: Label of the object whose world motion to compute.

frame_a.description: Start frame (default: first frame where target is present).

frame_b.description: End frame (default: last frame where target is present).

name: orient_facing
description:
Determine which direction an object is FACING from a single frame — a holistic, majority-voted VLM

read (no reconstruction). Uses the FULL image and votes over several reworded reads to de-bias.
perspective='egocentric' re-expresses left/right/front/back into the object's own frame.

image.description:
Path to the frame image to read the object's facing from (use the FULL frame, not a
crop).

target.description: The object whose facing direction to determine (e.g. 'the person', 'the car').

perspective.description:
'camera' = facing as YOU see it; 'egocentric' = re-expressed in the object's own
frame ('imagine you are X').

votes.description:
Self-consistency votes: asks the same neutral question N times and majority-votes to de-
bias. Default 3.

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: plan_exploration
description:
Given a target and the current scene, decide the next STRUCTURAL exploration move: (a) `spin_scan` —

turn ~360° in place to raise this room's coverage; (b) `traverse_gateway` — head to a door/corridor
pointing into an unobserved sector, then re-observe; (c) `go_forward` — no gateway, no target in
view; advance to a new vantage; (d) `found` — target already in scene, hand off to plan_navigation.
Pure geometry, no VLM. Complements `plan_active_search` (small local left/right) with structural
reasoning across rooms.

target.description: Object label we want to find (e.g. 'bed', 'conference room 302').

budget_moves.description: Max steps in the returned skill_sequence.

spin_coverage_deg.description: If current coverage_deg < this, prefer spin_scan first.

name: render_scene_views
description:
Render the scene's instances as orthographic 2D views (wireframe cuboids) from canonical faces —

DEFAULT front + top(BEV); add left/right only if a task needs more angles. Lets you 'look from
another angle' at the reconstructed layout. Needs a `scene` from build_scene.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene (alternative to `scene`).

faces.description: Which orthographic faces to render: front / top (=bev) / left / right. Default front+top.

frame.description: Frame whose instances to render (default: aggregate/available).

name: scene_map
description:
Structured scene-level views: 'cognitive_map' (grid layout of objects), 'appearance_order' (objects

by first-appearance frame), 'locate_event' (frames where an event/action occurs — temporal
localization), 'diff_frames' (what appeared/disappeared/moved between two frames). Needs a `scene`.

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene.

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: select_keyframes
description:
Pick the most informative frame indices: 'uniform' (evenly spaced), 'motion' (most diverse camera

viewpoints), 'coverage' (frames where a target is best visible), 'covisibility' (frames where
multiple objects are co-visible). Needs a `scene` except for 'uniform'.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (needed for motion/coverage/covisibility).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene.

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: triangulate
description:
Two-view triangulation of `target`'s world position from frames a and b — more accurate than

monocular depth_m WHEN the camera moved between them. Returns world_xz + triangulation_angle_deg +
reliable; if angle < 8° the baseline is too small — fall back to depth_m (Pattern A). Needs a
`scene` from build_scene.

scene.description: The `scene` object from build_scene (JSON object or JSON string).

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene (alternative to `scene`).

target.description: Label of the object to triangulate (must be present in both frames).

frame_b.description: Second frame index (needs real camera baseline vs frame_a).

name: verify_grounding
description:
Independently VERIFY a grounding: ask the VLM whether the region in `bbox` really shows `label`. Run

before finalizing any distance/relation conclusion — a wrong bbox is the #1 cause of a flipped
spatial answer. Returns a match verdict + confidence.

label.description: The label the region is claimed to show (e.g. 'chair').

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: view_reason
description:
Reason from an OBJECT's viewpoint (not the camera): 'scene_layout' (all objects from viewpoint's

perspective), 'from_viewpoint' (describe targets relative to viewpoint), 'visible_from' (is target
visible from viewpoint + direction/distance), 'line_of_sight' (is the view clear or occluded).
Object-perspective mirrors left/right vs the camera. Needs a `scene`.

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene.

viewpoint.description: The object whose perspective to reason from (e.g. 'the person').

model.description: Override the VLM model (default: from env).

name: visualize_bev
description:
Top-down BEV. Preferred: pass `scene` from build_scene + a `viewpoint` — the plot draws a DASHED

forward/right cross-hair with Front/Back/Left/Right quadrant labels centred on that viewpoint
(camera frame OR virtual viewpoint like 'stand at X facing Y'), so left/right/front/behind is a
direct read of which quadrant an object sits in — no manual Pattern-B trig. Also shows camera pitch
as an annotation (if |pitch|≥20° the BEV forward/back is flagged unreliable). Legacy: raw point
cloud via points_file / points_b64 still works.

scene.description:
`scene` object from build_scene (JSON or dict). Preferred input; instances/cameras drive
the plot.

scene_file.description: Path to a JSON file holding the scene (alternative to `scene`).

viewpoint.description:
Draw a DASHED forward/right cross-hair with Front/Back/Left/Right quadrant labels
centred on a viewpoint. {frame:N}=camera frame N; virtual viewpoint =
{at:[x,z]|label|{frame,label}, facing:label|[x,z]|heading_deg}. For 'facing the OPPOSITE
direction of X' questions, use `facing_away:label|[x,z]|heading_deg` (the tool auto-adds
180°); do NOT try to hand-derive the reverse angle. Turn any 'from X's perspective / left-
right/front-behind' question into reading the object's quadrant.

points_b64.description: Legacy: base64 numpy array of 3D points.

labels.description: Labels for each mask object (legacy point-cloud path).

resolution.description: BEV grid resolution in meters per pixel (legacy path).

name: image_search
description:
Reverse image search using an image file path (or a public image URL). Returns similar images

with their source URLs, titles, and descriptions. Local images require allow_public_upload=true
and are uploaded to the third-party public host uguu.se; their contents leave the machine and
become publicly accessible. Use this (and/or web_search) to CONFIRM any specific identification
— model/species/place/person/event — before you answer; appearance alone is not proof. Grab the
frame to search with save_view (don't run ffmpeg yourself).

image_path.description: Absolute path to the image file to search, OR a public http(s) image URL.

bbox.description: Bounding box [x1, y1, x2, y2] in relative coordinates (0-1000). Optional.

allow_public_upload.description:
Explicit consent to upload a local image (or cropped copy) to the
third-party public host uguu.se. Required whenever image_path is local or bbox requires
re-uploading a public URL.

name: web_extractor
description:
Crawl and extract content from web pages, with optional summarization. Returns the extracted

text or a summary focused on the specified goal.

urls.description: URLs to crawl and extract content from.

goal.description: What information to extract or focus on.

api_key.description:
API key for the selected search backend (defaults to its backend-specific
environment key).

name: web_search
description:
Search the internet for text information. Returns search results with titles, snippets, and

URLs.

queries.description: List of search queries to execute.

api_key.description:
API key for the selected search backend (defaults to its backend-specific
environment key).

name: transcribe_audio
description:
Transcribe local audio/video through Magpie. Choose provider/model; the default uses

Bailian Token Plan. language is a language code such as zh or en. SRT timestamps retain
the upstream tool's coarse 60-second chunk boundaries. Provider keys stay in Magpie.
Explicit enable_itn is supported only for legacy Qwen3-ASR models.

file_path.description: Existing local audio or video file.

model.description: Magpie provider/model identifier; defaults to Bailian Token Plan ASR.

start_time.description: Start offset in seconds, default zero.

end_time.description: End offset in seconds, default full duration.

format.description: Output format: srt, text, or json.

language.description: Language code such as zh or en; omit for detection.

enable_itn.description: Optional normalization flag for legacy Qwen3-ASR only.

api_key.description: Omit when connected; provider credentials are managed by Magpie.

name: synthesize_speech
description:
Generate speech through Magpie and save an audio artifact. output_path must be a new

absolute file path. voice is required; Bailian Token Plan supports longanhuan_v3.6.
Choose provider/model. Compatible providers use /audio/speech; Bailian uses Magpie's
native API relay. Billing follows the selected provider; no provider key is accepted.

output_path.description: New absolute audio file path in an existing directory.

voice.description: Provider voice identifier; Token Plan supports longanhuan_v3.6.

model.description: Magpie provider/model identifier; defaults to Bailian Token Plan TTS.

format.description: Output audio format: wav, mp3, or pcm.
